subject: Banking
title: Chatbots and Virtual Assistants
description: Learn Chatbots and Virtual Assistants in one minute.

hook.text: Bank of America's virtual assistant Erica has handled over 1.5 billion customer interactions since 2018.

buildup.text: Banking chatbots handle balance inquiries, payment scheduling, spending insights, and dispute filing.

discovery.text: Large language models now let chatbots understand complex requests.

twist.text: Air Canada's chatbot gave a customer incorrect refund information.

climax.text: AI assistants reduce costs but create liability. When the bot makes a mistake, the bank still owns the consequences.

punchline.text: 1.5 billion interactions, zero breaks. But one wrong promise creates liability.

quiz.question: What legal issue arose from Air Canada's chatbot?
options: The airline was held legally responsible for incorrect information the chatbot provided

details.summary: Banks are deploying AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants to handle routine customer inquiries, process transactions, and provide financial advice, reducing call center costs while offering instant 24/7 service across digital channels.
details.whyItMatters: Chatbots handle over 80 percent of routine banking inquiries at a fraction of the cost of human agents. As AI improves, virtual assistants are evolving from simple FAQ bots into personalized financial advisors.
takeaways: Bank of America's Erica virtual assistant has served over 1.5 billion requests
Chatbots reduce customer service costs by up to 30 percent
Advanced chatbots can now handle complex tasks like dispute resolution

faq.question: Can chatbots handle complex banking problems?
faq.answer: Increasingly, yes. Modern AI chatbots can process disputes, explain transactions, suggest products, and even detect financial stress. But they still escalate unusual situations to human agents when the conversation exceeds their training.

faq.question: Do customers prefer chatbots or human agents?
faq.answer: For simple tasks like balance checks and transfers, customers increasingly prefer the speed of chatbots. For complex problems or emotional situations like fraud, most customers still strongly prefer speaking with a human agent.
